summary: Iteration 4 testing: AI assistant + Community (auth, showcase, files, forum, chat WS) + regression. Wrote pytest suite (26 tests, all passing after fixes). Fixed 5 ObjectId-leak 500-errors in /app/backend/routers/community.py. Frontend largely works; AI assistant returns real LLM replies, but Emergent badge overlay intercepts AI launcher clicks for normal users.

ui_bugs.issue: The 'Made with Emergent' badge (#emergent-badge) sits at fixed bottom-right and overlaps the AI launcher button (data-testid='ai-launcher' at fixed bottom-6 right-6). Playwright reports pointer-events intercepted on every real click; only force-click via JS bypasses it. Real users cannot reliably open the AI panel because the lower ~60% of the launcher is covered by the badge.

When a signed-in buyer switches to the 'makers-only' channel via data-testid='chat-channel-makers-only', the UI renders 'Sign in to join the live chat' instead of an explicit 'makers only — restricted' message. WebSocket is correctly closed with 4403, but the user-facing copy is misleading because the user is already signed in.

issues: AI launcher position collides with Emergent corner badge (z-index 60 vs badge). Move launcher to bottom-24 right-6 or bottom-6 left-6.

action_items: Reposition AI launcher so it does not overlap the Emergent badge (e.g. bottom-24 right-6, or bottom-6 left-6). Today the badge intercepts real-user clicks on the launcher.

Improve makers-only blocked-state copy. When a buyer (signed in, role=buyer) switches to chat-channel-makers-only, render 'Makers only — this channel is restricted to verified makers.' instead of the generic 'Sign in to join the live chat'.
(Optional code-quality) Add a small `_strip_id(doc)` helper or use `{'_id': 0}` on returned docs, instead of repeating `doc.pop('_id', None)` after every insert_one — applies to all routers.
critical_code_review_comments: BUG (FIXED): /app/backend/routers/community.py — five endpoints inserted a dict via insert_one and then returned the same dict, leaking the mutated ObjectId and producing 500s on serialization. Affected: _upsert_buyer (used by /api/community/auth/magic/verify and /api/community/auth/google), POST /api/community/showcase, POST /api/community/files, POST /api/community/forum, POST /api/community/forum/{id}/reply. Patched by popping '_id' before return.
Note: routers/community.py is ~470 lines but still focused; if it grows, split chat WS into its own module.
AI router uses model 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929' (Anthropic via emergentintegrations) — confirmed reachable; multi-turn via session_id verified end-to-end.
Buyer role enforcement on /community/me, /maker/me, /community/showcase POST, /community/files POST, /community/forum POST is correct (401 vs 403 split is right).
WebSocket /api/ws/chat/{channel} correctly closes 4403 for buyer-on-makers-only and 4401 for missing token; broadcasts are persisted to chat_messages collection.

Run with: cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_iter4_ai_community.py -v --asyncio-mode=auto. The AI test does a real Claude call (3-8s). The AI launcher overlay-by-Emergent-badge bug is reproducible — open https://active-project-4.preview.emergentagent.com/ and try to click the bottom-right launcher; the click is intercepted by a.id='emergent-badge'.
rca of the issue: Root cause of the 500 errors: motor/pymongo's insert_one mutates the input dict in-place to add Mongo's _id (ObjectId). The handlers returned that same dict directly, so FastAPI's JSON encoder hit ObjectId and raised. Fix: pop '_id' before returning, or build the response dict without _id. Pattern applied to 5 sites in routers/community.py.
